summary: The remaining screen reaches pray.c prayer_done()’s co-aligned p_type-3 altar branch. C calls water_prayer(TRUE), which changes the ordinary water on the altar to holy water and emits “The potion on the altar glows light blue for a moment.” JS records note_unported("pray.c water_prayer") and continues into pleased(), so its “You feel…” line appears at the space that C uses to continue the prior prayer-completion pager. This is a missing whole-function source port in pray.c, not a generic pager-rendering defect. The preceding pray_revive() return is discarded and no revival candidate is present. The water_prayer() Boolean is consumed by the separate p_type-2 prayer_done() branch and must remain part of any broader caller wiring.

source.branch: In prayer_done(), p_type == 3 (coaligned and good-standing), outside Gehennom and standing on an altar with visible eligible floor POT_WATER, the source invokes water_prayer(TRUE); that helper blesses the water, marks its blessing knowledge, and emits the light-blue glow message before pleased().
callers: cmd.c's pray command dispatches to pray.c dopray(); the recorded #pray command reaches the same production handler.
pray.c dopray() installs prayer_done() as the after-move callback for the three-turn prayer; prayer_done() is the production caller of water_prayer().
In prayer_done() p_type 3 on an altar, C discards pray_revive() and water_prayer(TRUE) results, then calls pleased(). This is the reached caller branch for this case.

C prayer_done() also calls water_prayer(FALSE) in the p_type 0 and p_type 1 altar branches, discarding the result, and in the p_type 2 branch where its Boolean return selects the penalty path versus pleased().
The JavaScript route is js/cmd.js dopray dispatch -> js/pray.js dopray() -> prayer_done(); its current p_type-3 branch records the water_prayer gap and then calls pleased().
dependencies: pray.c water_prayer(boolean) at lines 1387-1412 scans level.objects[u.ux][u.uy], changes eligible POT_WATER blessed/cursed/bknown fields, prints only when visible water changed, and returns whether any water changed. The p_type-2 prayer_done() caller consumes that Boolean at pray.c:2327; p_type 0, 1, and 3 discard it. Preserve that return contract when wiring callers.

Before water_prayer(TRUE), p_type 3 calls pray_revive() and discards its Boolean result. JS records note_unported("pray.c pray_revive"). Its C body only revives a tame non-minion corpse/statue on the altar tile; this recording’s reached visible output is the water helper glow, and no corpse/statue candidate is introduced by the recipe.

After water_prayer(TRUE), C calls pleased(alignment); JS has a ported pleased() whose first message starts “You feel that…”. Skipping the earlier water message advances to that page at step 54, explaining the Y-versus-T screen and pager cursor shift. The saved diagnostic also records the first unpaired JS RNG entry rn2(3)=0 after C has no further logged call at that boundary; treat that as a downstream continuation effect to remeasure after water_prayer is wired.

js/pray.js currently has explicit UnsupportedPrayerError branches for p_type 0, 1, and 2. The p_type-2 consumed-return caller is not reached by this case; if broader prayer_done() wiring is selected, carry its water_prayer(FALSE) Boolean branch rather than dropping it.
nethack-c/patches/README.md lists deterministic time/seed, stable sorting, RNG logging, and terminal capture patches; these recorder patches do not change prayer or altar-water gameplay behavior.
